subject: Kestrel: runway validation for dedicated pool — provisional allocation request
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Capacity Planning <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Sales Ops <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, ML Infra <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kestrel: runway validation for dedicated pool — provisional allocation request

Team —

Late-stage ask from Kestrel (see below). They want a firm-ish runway for a Q3 GA that will start small and ramp quickly over 12 weeks. They asked us to confirm an internal availability check and a 30-day provisional hold for a dedicated pool while contracts finalize.

High-level numbers from Kestrel (external): 10 steady concurrent workers at ~1.2k tokens/s aggregate, peak concurrency bursts to 30 workers during spikes. Model: open-llama-70B variant they plan to quantize to 4-bit. Estimated token volumes are in the attached spreadsheet — rough guidance is 150M tokens/month initially, ramping.

Asks:
- Can Capacity confirm whether we can provision an isolated 8–12 A100-equivalent GPU pool (or an equivalent mix of A100/4090/V100 resources if needed) for a provisional hold starting 2029-06-01?
- If a provisional hold is possible, please include expiration date and what migration/fallback options we should prepare for.
- Any suggested quantization/packing recommendations that would materially change the node count?

I recommend we keep this to a 30-day provisional hold (auto-expire) unless leadership approves longer. Ben/Aditya — can you own the signed-later coordination with Procurement/Legal if Capacity signs off?

Thanks,
Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: kestrel_estimated_usage.xlsx (spreadsheet — forecast)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Apr 2029 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kestrel: runway validation for dedicated pool — provisional allocation request

Chloe —

I can run a fast availability sweep and open an ops ticket, but a few clarifying data points will change the outcome:
- Are they expecting single-model serving (dedicated weights in memory) or multi-tenant with fallbacks?
- What is the acceptable latency SLO? 95th perc target?
- Do they need KV cache persistence (sticky sessions) between requests?

From the spreadsheet it looks like their steady-state compute is ~8–10 80GB-A100 equivalents if they leave the 70B in FP16; quant to 4-bit would likely cut that to ~4–6 equivalents depending on perf delta. If they plan to use long context (8k+ tokens) that increases memory needs.

I will open INF-9123 and run an inventory check across our hosted and Dedicated pools. If Capacity can carve a provisional pool, provisional hold rules we usually apply: 30-day soft hold, requires a 25% commit or signed LOI to extend to 60 days. Will confirm TTL and exact resource mapping after the sweep.

Opening ops ticket now and looping infra.

—Aditya

Related ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9123
From: Laura Chen <laura@kestrel.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@kestrel.ai, procurement@kestrel.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Apr 2029 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kestrel: runway validation for dedicated pool — provisional allocation request

Hi Chloe —

Thanks for the quick turn. Quick answers inline to Aditya's questions:
- Single-model serving initially; we will pin a 70B variant and do A/B quant to 4-bit in staging. No multi-tenant mixing planned.
- Target latency: 95th < 220ms for chat-style requests; burst tolerance up to 700ms acceptable during spikes.
- We will use a sticky prefix cache for session continuity; KV cache persistence preferred but not mandatory on day 1.

I've attached a cleaned forecast and a simple ramp plan. We can provide a signed LOI for a 3-month commitment if that helps extend a hold window.

Attachment: kestrel_estimated_usage.xlsx

Best,
Laura Chen
Head of Infrastructure, Kestrel AI
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Kestrel: runway validation for dedicated pool — provisional allocation request

Looping Capacity Ops —

Inventory sweep complete across Dedicated and Hosted pools. Short summary:
- We can provision an equivalent of 8 A100-80GB nodes by reassigning some reserved capacity (45% probability we need to swap specific SKU types).
- If Kestrel moves to 4-bit quantization, that reduces the needed physical GPUs to 4–6 nodes; we can likely satisfy that from spare Dedicated capacity without impact to current committed customers.
- Proposed provisional hold: 30-day soft hold starting 2029-06-01. Extension path: signed LOI (we'll accept the 3-month LOI Laura mentioned) → extend to 60 days; fully executed contract → convert to reserved capacity.

I attached a short term plan and the allocation window. Ops requires a formal Hold Ticket to reserve the nodes; I'll submit once Chloe confirms we should proceed. TTL on the soft hold will be 2029-07-01 EOD if no LOI submitted.

Attachments: provisional_allocation_terms.docx

Ben
Director, Sales Ops
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2029 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kestrel: runway validation for dedicated pool — provisional allocation request

Technical notes for planning:
- If Kestrel intends to use 8k context and 4-bit quantization, recommend the following packing: 2x A100-80GB per 70B shard with mixed precision kernels; this gives the best balance of latency and memory headroom for bursty traffic.
- Suggest enabling prefix KV caching with an eviction TTL of 15m for startup traffic; this will lower per-token compute and reduce burst node count requirement.
- For the provisional pool, configure auto-scale floor at 4 nodes and ceiling at 12 nodes with immediate burst-to-ceiling on detected traffic patterns (subject to Capacity throttle policy).
- Ops note: ensure GPU tenancy isolation and log-level tracing for the first 30 days (billing and perf telemetry tagged 'KST-2029-42').

I'll coordinate with Aditya on exact node SKU mapping once the ops ticket is open.

—Neha
Senior ML Infra Engineer
